title: Lift both humanize number modules past 72 percent kill rate
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 338 mutants in humanize/number.py and 62 in humanize/filesize.py of humanize==4.9.0, and the score is the MINIMUM kill rate of the two modules -- overshooting one module cannot compensate for neglecting the other. From scratch under work/gc-353/tests/, build suites for ordinal, intcomma, intword, apnumber, fractional, scientific, clamp, metric, and naturalsize across binary, decimal, and gnu formats, including negative numbers, boundary magnitudes, and precision arguments. Track both per-module rates on every grading run and aim work at whichever module is behind. Fail-closed grading: red baseline, suite slower than 4 seconds, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift in either module scores min_module_kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi humanize==4.9.0 (targets under mutation: humanize/number.py and humanize/filesize.py)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-353/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-353/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-353/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-353/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-353/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Per-module kill rates are recorded for every grading run and the plan names which module the next iteration targets and why.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
